I’m Maya Chen calling to sort out several trips, and I want you to keep track of everything so I don’t have to repeat myself.
Let’s start with my round-trip reservation C4C633.
I want to cancel it because my plans changed, but first confirm whether the entire trip is eligible.

summary: A fifteen-turn flight-management marathon for Maya Chen: cancel round-trip C4C633 (T1-T2), audit and cancel one-way EC4C1C (T3), reconcile a self-introduced inconsistency (T4-T5), change booking A2CBB0 to a cheaper flight (T6), and run three new-booking search/confirm loops for SEA→SFO, JFK→MIA, and a LAX→SFO comparison (T7-T14), closing with a recap (T15). The run's signature pattern is a persistent instruction-compliance gap: the user asks for a pre-booking summary or a prior-booking confirmation first and the agent repeatedly skips straight to the next action — the user says "you skipped" at T5, T8, T11, T12, T13, and T14. The agent's redeeming moments are two genuine self-corrections: T5 reconciles having listed EC4C1C as active immediately after cancelling it, and T6 admits its earlier $75 change-fee estimate was wrong once the free-change window applied. As a CONTROL baseline the uncorrected defects are the self-introduced active/cancelled inconsistency at T3, the books-before-summarizing behavior at T10 and T13 (executed despite an explicit "summarize one more time" instruction), and the repeated failure across T11-T13 to give the SEA→SFO confirmation the user demanded before each new task. Every turn fires only generic other calls with zero retrieval, so all the fare and booking confirmations are self-reported.

findings.title: Skip-the-summary is the dominant failure mode
findings.body: At T10 and T13 the agent executes a booking without the "summarize the exact flight and total charge one more time" step the user explicitly required, and at T11-T13 it skips the requested prior-booking confirmation. The quote-level view shows these turns jump directly to Executing/Grounding with no preceding Evaluate › Plan-verification move — the pre-action check the user kept asking for is simply absent.

findings.title: Two real self-corrections stand out
findings.body: T5 ("You're right, I rushed past the reconciliation") and T6 ("I had originally estimated a $75 change fee, but the system applied the free change window") are Reflection › Self-Correct moves — both reactive to being caught, but genuine, and distinct from the ungrounded confidence elsewhere.

findings.title: A self-introduced data inconsistency
findings.body: T3 lists EC4C1C among active flight bookings in the same response that cancels it — a contradiction the agent created itself, only reconciled one turn later at T5. The granular tags separate the cancellation action from the erroneous active-list, which the turn-level summary blurs.
